extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_short: handling application abandonment and reply periods
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when a patent application is abandoned, how reply periods run and may be reset, requirements and procedures for express abandonment, petitions to reset periods, and petitions to revive abandoned applications under applicable MPEP rules and CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to reply during shortened statutory period results in abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a reply during the shortened statutory period results in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.135; examiner should notify applicant using Notice of Abandonment (PTOL-1432). Late amendments are endorsed on the file wrapper but not entered. See MPEP § 711.02 and form paragraphs (e.g., 7.90, 7.98.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: NO EXTENSIONS OF TIME AFTER PAYMENT OF ISSUE FEE
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory (nonextendable) time period for payment of the issue fee is 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151). Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are NOT available to correct outstanding informalities at time of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informalities (drawing corrections, supplemental/corrected declarations) must be corrected and the issue fee paid within the 3-month period. If issue fee is paid, withdrawal from issue requires petition under 37 CFR 1.313 (see MPEP §1308).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two periods running (statutory vs. limited time action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes two different periods for reply run against an application: the regular statutory period and a limited period set in a subsequent Office action; the running of the first period is not suspended or affected by an ex parte limited time action or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2305.03 for exceptions. When claims are copied from a patent, see Ex parte Milton and MPEP §2305.02 for which date controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying patent claims does not necessarily constitute a reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims are copied from a patent and all these claims are rejected there results a situation with two reply periods; the date of the last unanswered Office action on claims other than the copied patent claims is the controlling date of the statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Milton, 63 USPQ 132 (P.O. Super Exam. 1938) and MPEP §2305.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration on Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: When the last day for taking action or paying any fee falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken or fee paid on the next succeeding business day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory basis: 35 U.S.C. 21; implementing regulation: 37 CFR 1.7(a)-(b). Federal holidays under 5 U.S.C. 6103(a) listed; provisional application 12-month period extended if anniversary falls on weekend/holiday (see 37 CFR 1.53(c) and MPEP §201.04(b)). Examiners should check if the last day was a holiday when an amendment is filed shortly after expiration and endorse file wrapper accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations when reply period is reset or restarted for defective Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a citation is incorrect or an Office action contains another defect and this error is called to the Office's attention within 1 month of the mail date, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected, if requested by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If error is brought within the reply period but more than 1 month after mailing, the Office will set a new period substantially equal to the time remaining (new period must be at least 1 month) running from the date error corrected. If error is called to attention after expiration, period will not be restarted and extension fee required. See MPEP §707.05(g) and §707.13 for remailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redating when an action is remailed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it becomes necessary to remail any action, the action should be correspondingly redated, as the remailing date establishes the beginning of the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte Gourtoff and related MPEP sections apply. Supplementary actions after rejection establishing new explanations also establish a new date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to reset period due to late receipt of an Office action (criteria A–C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date of receipt at the correspondence address when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of receipt, (B) a substantial portion of the set reply period had elapsed on receipt (e.g., at least 1 month of a 2- or 3-month reply period), and (C) petition includes evidence showing date of receipt and a statement explaining the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to decide such petitions may be delegated to the TC Director where action was mailed by a Technology Center. See Notice “Petition to reset a period for response due to late receipt of a PTO action.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to reset period due to postmark date later than mail date (criteria A–C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the reply period to run from the postmark date shown on the mailing envelope when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of receipt, (B) the reply period was for payment of the issue fee or was 1 month/30 days, and (C) the petition includes evidence of receipt, copy of envelope showing postmark, and a statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10 apply to filing these petitions. The Office will scrutinize circumstances that suggest delay after receipt rather than delay in the mail or Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment defined and insufficiency of reply (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135 specifies an application becomes abandoned if applicant fails to reply within the time period (including if the reply is insufficient — not a 'complete and proper reply' as the condition of the case may require).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution to save an application must include the complete and proper reply. Admission or refusal to admit amendments after final rejection or amendments not responsive to the last action will not save the application from abandonment. See MPEP §714.02–§714.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment requirements (37 CFR 1.138)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be expressly abandoned by filing a written declaration of abandonment identifying the application; the declaration must be signed by a party authorized under §1.33(b)(1),(b)(3), or (b)(4), except in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered attorney or agent not of record acting in representative capacity under §1.34(a) when filing a continuing application may expressly abandon the prior application as of the filing date granted the continuing application. Express abandonment may not be recognized before date of issue/publication unless actually received in time to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment and examination of express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a letter of express abandonment complying with 37 CFR 1.138 is received, examiner should acknowledge it and indicate whether it complies with 37 CFR 1.138; use Notice of Abandonment form PTO-1432 and check appropriate boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the letter does not comply, send a fully explanatory letter. Use form paragraphs 7.88 (acknowledge) and 7.89 (improper) as guidance. With some exceptions (e.g., abandonment filed with a continuing application), express abandonments must be signed by all inventors or owners of entire interest or attorney/agent of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment cancelling all claims is not express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the filing date canceling all of the claims, even if signed by applicant and assignee, is not an express abandonment but is regarded as nonresponsive and should not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be notified as explained in MPEP §714.03 to §714.05 (citing Ex parte Lasscell).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment to avoid publication — timing and petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking to abandon to avoid publication must submit a declaration of express abandonment by way of a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) including the fee in §1.17(h) in sufficient time to permit recognition and removal from publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition will generally not be granted unless received more than four weeks prior to projected publication date; unlikely to be effective within four weeks. See MPEP §711.05 and §1308; Box PGPUB-ABN recommended for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to take required action during statutory period — examiner procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed after expiration of the statutory period, the application is abandoned and examiner should notify applicant using PTOL-1432; late amendment is endorsed but not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.90 and 7.98.02 may be used. Do not mail abandonment letter until extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) has expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive — unavoidable vs. unintentional grounds (37 CFR 1.137)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive must be accompanied by the required reply, appropriate showing (that the delay was unavoidable under 1.137(a) or unintentional under 1.137(b)), any required terminal disclaimer under 1.137(c), and the petition fee in 1.17(l)/(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For unavoidable delay, show (1) the entire delay was unavoidable and (2) any delay between abandonment and petition filing was unavoidable. For unintentional delay, include a statement that the entire delay was unintentional; Commissioner may require additional information. No consideration of substance until fee received. Terminal disclaimer required for certain applications (designs, pre-June 8, 1995 utility/plant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of reply — abandonment can result despite a filed reply
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be abandoned where applicant's reply is within the period but is not fully responsive to the Office action (i.e., insufficiency of reply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.91 to inform applicant and suggest extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a); if reply appears bona fide with inadvertent omission, use form paragraph 7.95 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations causing abandonment (enumerated examples A–I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain specific circumstances often arise and should be specially noted as they may cause abandonment (A) copying claims from a patent not suggested by the Office, (B) withdrawal/failure to prosecute an appeal, (C) dismissal of appeals or civil action without appropriate amendment, (D) suggested claims for interference near end of reply period, (E) FWC application issues, (F) filing a CPA under former rules, (G) improperly filed RCE prior to Board decision, (H) RCE filed while reply outstanding to final action without required submission, (I) improper RCE prior to payment of issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2305, §706.07(h), §201.06, §1215–§1216 and related sections for detailed treatment; improper filings may not toll prior time periods and can result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings (35 U.S.C. 120 context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are terminated for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 120 when (A) issue fee not paid and application abandoned (proceedings terminated as of date issue fee was due), (B) application loses an interference to all claims, (C) after decision by the Board, and (D) after decision by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination means the earlier application is no longer copending for 35 U.S.C. 120 purposes; see MPEP §711.02(c) for further detail on dates and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of holding of abandonment; examiner authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may ask for reconsideration of a holding of abandonment or petition for revival under 1.137. The primary examiner may reverse a prior holding as to whether an amendment received during the period was responsive and act on an application previously held abandoned (not a revival but a holding that application was never abandoned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §711.03(a) and §714.03 for procedures and limits on examiner authority.
